U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson barred the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security from pressing local election officials to purge registered voters, withhold their ballots, or set their midterm ballots aside solely because they appear on a federal list of suspected noncitizen voters. At 2 am on Sunday, our clocks will fall back one hour, returning us to standard time for the next four and a half months or so. stories.summary: Prediction markets blew three big elections this week, a bad look for platforms pitching themselves to investors as hedges against global risk. Kalshi and Polymarket both gave Brazilian conservative Flávio Bolsonaro a 4-in-5 chance of winning; he lost to the progressive incumbent, costing anyone who traded Brazil’s currency and stocks. The markets also overrated Netanyahu’s challenger in Israel, where the race is still too close to call — and where a series of suspicious bets elicited an investigation by Polymarket. In Serbia (emerging-market investors need good information, too!), Kalshi gave the heavily favored incumbent strongman 75% odds as late as election day. He lost. Kalshi has touted the accuracy of its markets to win over institutional investors. A hedge that doesn’t work is doubly bad: useless expensive. — Liz Hoffman
